::: {#exr-bikeshare-fit}

#### Fit a Poisson regression to bike rentals

The [`Bikeshare` data](#sec-bikeshare-lab) count the bikes rented in each of many hours.
Each count covers one hour,
so every count has the same [exposure magnitude](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-exposure).
Consider a [Poisson regression model](poisson-regression.qmd#def-poisson-regression) of the hourly count `bikers`
on the [covariates](model-validation.qmd#def-covariate) `temp`, `workingday`, and `weathersit`,
with `clear` as the [reference level](data.qmd#def-reference-level) of `weathersit`.

::: {.callout-tip}

#### Hint

In R, `glm()` with `family = poisson` [fits](model-validation.qmd#def-fitted-model) the model.
In Python, the `statsmodels` function `smf.glm()` fits it with `family=sm.families.Poisson()`.
Both code `weathersit` as one [dummy variable](data.qmd#def-dummy-variable) for each level except the [reference level](data.qmd#def-reference-level).

:::

[Estimate](estimation.qmd#def-estimate) the coefficient of each [covariate](model-validation.qmd#def-covariate) in the model.

:::
